newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro to sell software in Russia - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro to sell software in Russia - WSJ.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc plans to sell encryption software from a Russian supplier to overseas customers, a move that is likely to receive close scrutiny by the U.S. government, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said the transaction, involving a company formed by scientists from the former Soviet space program, skirts U.S. export regulations.
Sun Microsystems is expected to announce Monday that it will sell the data-security software from Elvis+ Co. Sun has a 10 percent equity stake in the Russian company.
The products are to be shipped to overseas customers from Sun distributors in third countries, which would keep them from coming under U.S. jurisdiction, the Journal said.
The export of powerful encryption products is prohibited under U.S. export-control laws on the grounds that terrorists and others would use it to evade surveillance.
